knowledge:
- key_parameters: inputNetwork=Path to a .net file or an R network object (igraph, graphNEL, matrix, data.frame) ;; edgeType=Type of edge, either "unweighted" or "weighted" ;; outputFormat=Format of output file: "nsm" (for NetGestalt), "gmt" (for GSEA), "msm" (for MatSAM), "multiple" (ruler, hmi, net, cct, and tsi files), or "none" ;; map_to_genesymbol=Logical, whether to transform IDs to gene symbols using biomaRt ;; organism=Organism of the input network (e.g., "hsapiens", "mmusculus", "rnorvegicus") ;; idType=ID type of input network, "auto" searches automatically (takes ~10 mins) ;; minModule=Minimum percentage of nodes in a module (default 0.003, min size 5, max 0.2) ;; stepIte=Logical, whether to test a range of random walk lengths (2 to maxStep) to find the optimal length ;; moduleSigMethod=Method to test non-random modular organization ("cutoff", "zscore", or "permutation") ;; modularityThr=Modularity score threshold for "cutoff" method (default 0.2) ;; edgeThr=Threshold of number of edges to stop execution if network is too big (default -1, recommended 300,000) ;; nodeThr=Threshold of number of nodes to stop execution if network is too big (default -1, recommended 12,000) ;; collapse_mode=Method to collapse duplicate IDs ("mean", "median", "maxSD", "maxIQR", "max", "min") ;; matNetMethod=Method to construct correlation network ("value", "rank", "directed")
- alternatives: Traditional hierarchical clustering (lacks leaf ordering optimization, statistical significance assessment of modules, and multi-scale hierarchical level specification). NetGestalt (external 1D visualization tool that takes NetSAM's "nsm" or "msm" output). GSEA (uses "gmt" output for module enrichment).
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing biological networks (e.g., protein-protein interaction, co-expression) to find hierarchical modules and an optimal 1D linear ordering of genes, or when starting with transcriptomics/expression matrices and wanting to build correlation networks (with or without bootstrapping) and identify modules associated with clinical/sample features or GO terms.
- pitfalls: Memory consumption is very high because seriation requires pairwise distances; 64-bit R is recommended with at least 8GB RAM for <10,000 nodes and 16GB RAM for >10,000 nodes. For large networks (edges > 200,000), set stepIte = FALSE to avoid extremely long runtimes. Automatic ID mapping (idType = "auto") can take up to 10 minutes depending on network connection speed. If network size exceeds edgeThr or nodeThr, the function will stop.

workflows.name: network_seriation_and_modularization
workflows.intent: Perform network seriation and modularization on an existing network file or object to identify hierarchical modules and optimal leaf ordering, and optionally analyze network properties.
input: network.net (network edge-list file where each row represents an edge with two node names and optional weight, separated by tab or space)
workflows.stages: 1. Run NetSAM to identify hierarchical modules and optimal leaf ordering. 2. Run NetAnalyzer to calculate network centrality measurements and plot their distributions.
workflows.code:
library("NetSAM")
inputNetworkDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleNetwork.net",package="NetSAM")
outputFileName <- paste(getwd(),"/NetSAM",sep="")
result <- NetSAM(inputNetwork=inputNetworkDir, outputFileName=outputFileName, outputFormat="nsm",
edgeType="unweighted", map_to_genesymbol=FALSE, organism="hsapiens", idType="auto", minModule=0.003,
stepIte=FALSE, maxStep=4, moduleSigMethod="cutoff", modularityThr=0.2, ZRanNum=10,
PerRanNum=100, ranSig=0.05, edgeThr=(-1), nodeThr=(-1), nThreads=3)

library("NetSAM")
inputNetwork <- system.file("extdata","exampleNetwork.net",package="NetSAM")
outputFileName <- paste(getwd(),"/NetSAM",sep="")
NetAnalyzer(inputNetwork,outputFileName,"unweighted")

workflows.name: matsam_correlation_modularization
workflows.intent: Construct a correlation network from an expression matrix, identify hierarchical modules, and find associations with sample features and GO terms in a single workflow.
input: expression.cct (gene expression matrix file with column names and gene IDs in the first column), sample_annotation.tsi (sample annotation file with feature names, types, and categories)
workflows.stages: 1. Test the format of the input expression matrix and sample annotation data. 2. Run MatSAM to construct the correlation network, identify modules, and calculate feature/GO associations.
workflows.code:
library("NetSAM")
inputMatDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleExpressionData.cct",package="NetSAM")
sampleAnnDir <- system.file("extdata","sampleAnnotation.tsi",package="NetSAM")
formatedData <- testFileFormat(inputMat=inputMatDir,sampleAnn=sampleAnnDir,collapse_mode="maxSD")

library("NetSAM")
inputMatDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleExpressionData.cct",package="NetSAM")
sampleAnnDir <- system.file("extdata","sampleAnnotation.tsi",package="NetSAM")
outputFileName <- paste(getwd(),"/MatSAM",sep="")
matModule <- MatSAM(inputMat=inputMatDir, sampleAnn=sampleAnnDir,
                    outputFileName = outputFileName, outputFormat="msm",
                    organism="hsapiens", map_to_symbol=FALSE, idType="auto", collapse_mode="maxSD", naPer=0.7, meanPer=0.8, varPer=0.8,
corrType="spearman", matNetMethod="rank",
valueThr=0.6, rankBest=0.003, networkType="signed", netFDRMethod="BH",
netFDRThr=0.05, minModule=0.003, stepIte=FALSE,
maxStep=4, moduleSigMethod="cutoff", modularityThr=0.2, ZRanNum=10, PerRanNum=100, ranSig=0.05, idNumThr=(-1), nThreads=3)

workflows.name: stepwise_correlation_network_analysis
workflows.intent: Manually construct a correlation network (or consensus network), identify modules, and perform feature and GO association analyses step-by-step.
input: expression.cct (gene expression matrix file with column names and gene IDs in the first column), sample_annotation.tsi (sample annotation file with feature names, types, and categories)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct a correlation network using MatNet (or a consensus network using consensusNet). 2. Run NetSAM on the constructed network. 3. Calculate associations between sample features and modules using featureAssociation. 4. Identify associated GO terms for modules using GOAssociation.
workflows.code:
library("NetSAM")
inputMatDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleExpressionData.cct",package="NetSAM")
matNetwork <- MatNet(inputMat=inputMatDir, collapse_mode="maxSD", naPer=0.7, meanPer=0.8, varPer=0.8,
corrType="spearman", matNetMethod="rank", valueThr=0.6, rankBest=0.003, networkType="signed",
netFDRMethod="BH", netFDRThr=0.05, idNumThr=(-1), nThreads=3)

library("NetSAM")
inputMatDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleExpressionData.cct",package="NetSAM")
data <- read.table(inputMatDir, header=TRUE, row.names=1, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
net <- consensusNet(data=data, organism="hsapiens",bootstrapNum=10, naPer=0.5, meanPer=0.8,varPer=0.8,method="rank_unsig",value=3/1000,pth=1e-6, nMatNet=2, nThreads=4)

library("NetSAM")
inputMatDir <- system.file("extdata","exampleExpressionData.cct",package="NetSAM")
sampleAnnDir <- system.file("extdata","sampleAnnotation.tsi",package="NetSAM")
data(NetSAMOutput_Example)
outputHtmlFile <- paste(getwd(),"/featureAsso_HTML",sep="")
featureAsso <- featureAssociation(inputMat=inputMatDir, sampleAnn=sampleAnnDir, NetSAMOutput=netsam_output, outputHtmlFile=outputHtmlFile, CONMethod="spearman", CATMethod="kruskal", BINMethod="ranktest", fdrmethod="BH",pth=0.05,collapse_mode="maxSD")

library("NetSAM")
data(NetSAMOutput_Example)
outputHtmlFile <- paste(getwd(),"/GOAsso_HTML",sep="")
GOAsso <- GOAssociation(NetSAMOutput=netsam_output, outputHtmlFile=outputHtmlFile, organism="hsapiens", fdrmethod="BH", fdrth=0.05, topNum=5)
